front.title: An Entity Attestation Token (EAT) Profile for Signed Pre-Silicon Hardware Security Evidence

abstract.t: Hardware security designs are increasingly assessed before fabrication: by gate-level leakage simulation, fault-injection simulation, formal proofs and equivalence checking. The results of these assessments are routinely copied into reports, slide decks and certification packages with no binding to the design that was assessed, the stimulus that was used, the conditions under which the numbers hold, or the platform that produced them. This document defines an Entity Attestation Token (EAT) profile for carrying such pre-silicon assessment results as signed Evidence. Every claim is classified as identifying the assessed artifact, describing a measured behavior, or describing the measurement conditions. A provenance claim, which states whether the signing key is rooted in hardware or software, is mandatory, and a simulated Trusted Platform Module is always reported as a software root. The profile is explicitly not a certification format: it records what was measured and under which envelope, so that a Relying Party can decide what the numbers are evidence of.
